summary.intent: Participate as the claude-code agent in a multi-agent RFD authoring session to review and refine a design document about agent memory lessons/experiences, then record a stance in the timeline file.
summary.outcome: The RFD was edited with concrete migration mapping rules, a scoring carve-out for legacy records, a verification bullet, and an open question about LLM extraction. A Turn 3 timeline entry was appended with stance 'approve'.

repo: The legacy memory store (memory-loop.json) contains 23 records, 6 of which are me-scoped, and none have a `source_signal` field — directly impacting migration logic.
The memoryloop package has a `generator.go` file handling fingerprint computation and an `owner_id`/`owner_email` owner translation scheme.
Migration from the legacy memory schema requires a three-branch `owner_id` translation logic based on the actual JSON store contents.
Migrated records with empty structured fields would be silently invisible under the new scoring logic without an explicit summary-fallback carve-out for `origin='manual'` records.

code.finding: Contains fingerprint computation logic and owner_email/owner_id fields relevant to migration mapping.
Core memoryloop implementation; source_signal field is absent from all existing records.

workflow: In multi-agent RFD sessions, agents must read both the RFD doc and the full timeline before forming an opinion, then edit the RFD and append a structured timeline entry.
Codebase investigation (reading files, running grep/bash) before editing an RFD ensures proposed migration rules are grounded in actual data rather than assumptions.
Stances should only be 'approve' if the agent genuinely agrees after their own edits; remaining open questions that are non-blockers do not prevent approval.

friction: The RFD's prior wording used vague 'nearest structured field' prose for migration mapping, requiring replacement with explicit pinned rules.
No `source_signal` field existed in any of the 23 legacy records, meaning the migration logic had to account for this absence explicitly.
open_items: Whether to optionally run a one-shot LLM extraction pass over legacy records to backfill structured fields (§13 open question — recommended to defer).
End-to-end verification that the summary-fallback scoring path for `origin='manual'` records with empty structured fields works correctly (§14 verification bullet added but not yet tested).
implementation_rationale: Pinned explicit mapping rules (summary=body, structured fields empty, legacy title/why/evidence preserved in legacy_import history row) were chosen over vague prose to make the migration deterministic and auditable.
A narrow summary-fallback carve-out for `origin='manual'` records was added to prevent migrated lessons from being active but never injected — which would be silently worse than the current behavior.
LLM extraction backfill was deferred to avoid scope creep in PR 1; it can be done as a follow-on once the migration schema is stable.
tradeoffs: Deferring optional LLM extraction over legacy records keeps PR 1 scope tight but means migrated records will have empty structured fields initially, relying on the summary-fallback path for injection.
Using a strict three-branch owner_id translation verified against actual store contents is more precise but tightly coupled to the current store's specific data shape.
codebase_patterns: Memory records use a `source_signal` field that is absent from all legacy records — new migration code must handle this absence explicitly.
Owner identity is tracked via `owner_id`/`owner_email` fields in the memoryloop generator, requiring a translation step during migration.
Fingerprints are recomputed under the new schema after migration, not carried over from legacy records.
